title: The Three Zones of a Flame
description: A candle flame hides three secret zones. Map them to reclaim the Guardian Flame's core ember.

content.value: A candle flame may look simple, but it has THREE different ZONES, each a different colour and temperature. Understanding them explains a lot about how fire works.

THREE ZONES OF A CANDLE FLAME

   🔵 OUTER zone   → blue, hottest, complete burning
   🟡 MIDDLE zone  → yellow, bright (luminous), moderate heat
   ⚫ INNER zone   → dark, coolest, unburnt wax vapour

(the wick sits in the dark inner zone)

The INNER (dark) zone, around the wick, is the COOLEST — it has unburnt wax vapour and little oxygen. The MIDDLE (yellow) zone is the LUMINOUS part that gives most of the light, where partial burning happens. The OUTER (blue) zone is the HOTTEST, where complete burning occurs with plenty of oxygen.

This is why gold and silver smiths use the OUTERMOST (blue) zone of a flame to melt metals — it is the hottest part, with the most complete combustion. The dark inner zone is actually the coolest part of the flame.
Surprising fact: the bright yellow middle is NOT the hottest part! The pale blue outer zone is hottest because burning is most complete there, with the most oxygen.
Key Takeaway: A candle flame has three zones — a cool dark inner zone (unburnt vapour), a bright yellow luminous middle zone, and the hottest blue outer zone where complete burning happens.

quiz.question: Which zone of a candle flame is the HOTTEST?
quiz.explain: The blue outer zone is hottest because burning is most complete there, with plenty of oxygen.

quiz.question: The dark innermost zone of a flame is…
options: the coolest part, with unburnt wax vapour
quiz.explain: The dark inner zone near the wick is the coolest and contains unburnt vapour.

quiz.question: Goldsmiths melt metals using the outer zone of a flame because it…
quiz.explain: The outermost blue zone is the hottest, so it is used for melting metals.
